summary: Patrick McAllister works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner, and became a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~2012).

Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Patrick Olivelle studied at Oxford (~1969–1972) and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974) under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University (1974–1991) and UT Austin (1991).
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Robert Buswell as a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar and teacher. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1830–1842) and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and instructed disciples such as Shenpen Nangwa and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities (PhD ~1991–1994), she served as associate professor and Asian Studies director at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).
Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul B. Donnelly specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, Lobsang Gyatso, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1997), and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a philosopher, Buddhist studies scholar, and religious studies author. He earned a PhD from the University of Tübingen (~1874–1876) and served as editor of The Open Court and The Monist (~1887/1890–1919).

Paul Copp is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Princeton (attested 2005) under Stephen F. Teiser. He has held positions at Western Michigan University, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe specializes in religious studies and Sinology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and later became a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies scholar educated at Nizam College, Presidency College Chennai, and Yale University (doctorate ~1927–1931). He taught at United Theological College (1932–1949) and directed the CISRS from 1956.

Paul David Numrich is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1992. By 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), the journal Wissen und Wandel (1955), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Union (1955).

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held professorships at INALCO (1931–1945), Collège de France (1946–1964), and directed the Hōbōgirin project (~1929–1979).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, learning under Christian Lassen. He served as a Privatdocent at the University of Berlin (1881–1887) and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, where he later led Asian Studies (~1976–2021), and served as head of the Pali Text Society.

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held academic posts at Michigan State University (attested 1992) and the University of Rochester (attested 2000).

Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held a long-term academic appointment at the University of California, San Francisco (~1960–2004).

Paul F. Knitter is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1970–1972), and held a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a Belgian historian who obtained his doctorate from the University of Liège (~1871–1875). He was a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) before becoming a professor (1883) and rector (1919) at Ghent University.
